procedure: Make three small holes at different heights in the side of a container.
Observe the water streams flowing out of the holes; each stream initially flows out normal to the surface.
Observe which stream hits the ground at the larger distance.
Discuss at which position the liquid has more pressure.
aim: To observe how liquid pressure changes with depth.

viva.question: In which direction does water initially flow out of a hole in the side of the container?
Which hole has the greatest liquid pressure?
viva.answer: The lowest hole, because it is at the greatest depth below the water surface.

viva.question: How does liquid pressure change with depth?
Why do the water streams curve downwards?
Does the stream from the lowest hole always hit the ground farthest away?
viva.answer: No. The horizontal distance depends on both the hole’s depth below the water surface and its height above the ground, so a middle stream may travel farthest.

apparatus: Pin or nail to make the holes
diagram: Draw a container partly filled with water, with three holes at different heights and curved water streams from them; label the water, the top hole “LOWEST PRESSURE”, and the lowest hole “HIGHEST PRESSURE”.
title: Pressure in liquids
precautions: Make the three holes small and at clearly different heights.
Keep the container upright and steady while observing.
Fill the container carefully to avoid spilling water.
Keep the area around the container clear and dry to prevent slipping.
result: The lowest hole has the greatest pressure because liquid pressure increases with depth. The stream that travels farthest depends on both the hole’s depth below the water surface and its height above the ground.
